name: Speed Ramp
summary: Time is the edit: 8× fast-forward through a week of dashboards, a snap to 1× on the drop, ¼× slow motion for the human decision, with a speed graph under every frame.
look: Warm paper frames with echo-frame trails, a giant coral speed readout and a dark editor-style time-remap strip whose playhead moves along a teal curve.

components.name: Speed graph
components.role: dark time-remap strip (8× / 1× / ¼×) with a coral playhead; the film’s spine

components.name: Speed readout
components.role: huge mono 8× / 1× / ¼× numeral in the corner, instantly readable

components.name: Echo frames
components.role: ghosted copies of moving UI showing fast-forward

components.name: Day chips
components.role: MON–FRI ticker that proves time is passing

components.name: Cursor onion trail
components.role: 4 fading cursors showing slow-motion movement toward the decision

components.name: Resolution chip
components.role: “Resolved in 6 min” green chip that closes the time story

motion.name: Fast-forward
motion.how: 8× section: every UI update lands on eighth notes (0.25 s at 120 BPM), linear ease, echo trails 5 frames deep

motion.name: Ramp knee
motion.how: 8× → 1× in 6 frames with a custom bezier (0.9, 0, 0.1, 1) so the change lands exactly on the drop; kick drum = snap

motion.name: Slow-mo hold
motion.how: 1× → ¼× over one bar (2 s, sine.inOut) into the proof, hold ¼× for 12 s, ramp back over one bar; graduated steps (1–2–4–2–1) feel natural

story: Hook: a week of dashboards races by at 8×, “And the drop still shipped on Friday.” Reveal: speed snaps to 1× on the drop and Acme Pulse lands sharp. Proof: ¼× slow motion as “Checkout conversion −18%” rises and the cursor crawls to Roll back. CTA: back to 1×, “Resolved in 6 min”, “Every metric. Every minute.”, Start free.
adapt: Record your product doing real work, then fast-forward the busywork your users do today and ramp down to slow motion on the one moment your product changes (the click, the approval, the result). The speed graph works with any product.

references.note: speed ramping: smooth speed changes within one shot

fit.risk: Speed ramps only read if the viewer can feel the change; without motion (echo frames, ticking clocks) the 8× and ¼× look the same in a still, and a slow section longer than about 8 s drags.
